summary.headline: Goldiam Q2 FY27 revenue rose 44% to Rs 2,916.6 mn and PAT rose 58% to Rs 494 mn, with H1 revenue up 50%.
summary.overview: Goldiam reported Q2 FY27 revenue of Rs 2,916.6 mn (up 44% YoY) and H1 revenue of Rs 6,553.2 mn (up 50%). EBITDA was Rs 736 mn (up 55.3%), with EBITDA margin up 176 bps YoY, and PAT was Rs 494 mn (up 58%). Management attributed growth to deeper and broader US retailer relationships amid vendor consolidation, and reported that origin (its retail brand) is reaching store-level break-even at a monthly revenue of about Rs 18-19 lakh. The company also declared an interim dividend of Rs 2 per share and plans to speed up origin store expansion in H2.

financial_highlights.change: up 55.3% YoY; margin up 176 bps YoY

financial_highlights.value: Rs 2 per share (100% of Rs 2 face value), Rs 301.11 mn total

financial_highlights.metric: Cash and cash equivalents incl. investments
Lab-grown diamond (LGD) jewelry share of export sales

financial_highlights.value: Rs 113 mn (about Rs 11.3-11.5 crore per management)

segments.name: B2B (US and international wholesale/retail customers)
segments.commentary: Majority of revenue, with about 85-90% retail channel and the rest wholesale. Growth came from deeper share with existing US retailers plus new wholesale, international (Middle East, Israel, Australia) accounts, with about USD 10-12 mn of sales from newly onboarded accounts so far.

segments.name: origin (B2C retail, India)
segments.commentary: 29 operational stores. Management said Q2 origin revenue was about Rs 11.3-11.5 crore with a loss of about Rs 3-3.5 crore at the EBITDA-type level. Regional revenue grew north of 20% QoQ on a similar store base, and monthly SSG was close to double digits from May to November.

guidance_outlook: Management expects strong growth in Q3 and Q4 and for the full year, with B2B order flow and US sell-through described as strong.
origin expansion to speed up from H1 pace through end of Q4 FY27; store-level break-even of about Rs 18-19 lakh monthly revenue; per-store investment about Rs 3-3.3 crore including inventory.
Management said the new margin level is expected to be sustained into Q3 following the hybrid casting model, excluding regulatory refunds received in Q2.
Management expects to be number one or two retailer in lab-grown diamond jewelry in its origin markets; Q4 call to give detailed FY28 store plan.
Management targets origin stores at Rs 4-5 crore annual revenue at maturity (Rs 2-2.5 crore for matured stores today, with a three-year target of Rs 5 crore).
capex_capacity: origin store count rose from 26 at Q1 call to 29 as of this call; new stores planned at Jayanagar (Bangalore, December) and HSR Layout (Bangalore, early next year).

Per origin store: capex about Rs 45-55 lakh, deposit about Rs 30-40 lakh, inventory and working capital about Rs 2-2.3 crore; total about Rs 3-3.3 crore. Larger high-street stores about 10% higher; smaller mall stores about 20% lower.
Target rent of Rs 3-5 lakh per month per store.
Management said fund raise (QIP) is complete and funding is available for expansion.
B2B requires no significant capex; spending is on inventory and working capital for new designs and accounts.
demand_pricing: Management said origin's ASP is broadly consistent, within plus or minus 10%; order book is not considered a meaningful metric because cycles run about 3 to 8 weeks.
Retail LGD pricing: management said no change, with pricing bands for VS, VVS and mixed categories within about 10% across retailers.
Wholesale LGD prices: management said prices are stable and in some categories up 5-15% over the last six months; wholesaler margins are about 25-35%, depending on client and payment mode.
Share gains are coming from smaller Indian and Hong Kong vendors being consolidated out by large US retailers (60-80+ stores or more, some with 500+ stores).
Management said the Q2 festive period was the single highest-sales day for origin so far, with demand picking up at the start of Q3.

qa_highlights.question: How is US B2B demand in the Q3 season and what drove the sharp growth beyond wallet share and vendor consolidation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited deeper presence with existing customers (more SKUs per retailer as designs are proven and expanded across doors) plus new wholesale, retail and international accounts, including Middle East and Israel. New bracelet and necklace categories are being sampled, with entry into key retailer accounts expected from Q4.

qa_highlights.question: How many origin stores will be opened in H2 and FY28, and what has been learned?
qa_highlights.answer: Expansion was slowed from May to focus on sales per store, with A/B tests on product, pricing, store format and size. Management said expansion will pick up to the end of Q4 FY27. A CRM system, website revamp and a jewelry purchase plan are being launched as sales enablers.

qa_highlights.question: What was origin's revenue in H1 and quarterly run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 was similar to Q1, at about Rs 3.3-3.5 crore per quarter (net, store level basis as stated).

qa_highlights.question: What is origin's SSG, and what are break-even economics per store?
qa_highlights.answer: SSG was close to double digits almost every month from May to November. Store-level monthly revenue break-even is about Rs 18-19 lakh; August was reported at break-even, and older stores such as Central 50 in Noida routinely exceed Rs 30 lakh a month.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company hedging currency risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Gold and diamonds are imported in USD and exports are invoiced in USD, giving a natural hedge; only the margin and labour are exposed. Board policy requires at least 50% of the net open exposure to be hedged.

qa_highlights.question: Why has order book stayed around Rs 225 crore, and how is growth split between existing and new customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said order book is not a meaningful metric given short cycles and daily e-commerce and international orders. Growth is mainly from existing accounts, with new accounts adding as a kicker; new US sales agents are being hired to target 2-3 accounts.

risks_watch: Customs and regulatory exposure on the US-India-US manufacturing model; management said it holds a US CBP ruling in its own name and that large peers face the same tariff ruling.
origin store economics: profitability depends on sustaining per-store break-even and maturing new stores (several are still in ramp-up); Q2 origin loss of about Rs 3-3.5 crore.
Working capital and inventory build for new designs; management says inventory build has historically led to revenue growth, but sell-through is not captured in order book.
Currency exposure on the 10-15% margin component, with at least 50% of open exposure hedged.
Q3 and Q4 execution on new bracelet and necklace categories and entry into key US retailer accounts.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on B2B growth and origin traction; management repeatedly described the outlook as strong for Q3 and Q4. It was more measured on origin, acknowledging "a lot more to do" and treating the Q4 call as the point for a detailed store plan. Management was evasive on order book and on whether certification would be needed for LGD in the long run.
key_quotes: Our top line growth of over 40% comes at a time when large US retailers are consolidating their vendor base.
we see no risk large peers like Goldiam are operating on the same same same same level accordingly and through the same tariff ruling from US CBP and we hope to continue moving forward
in fact keeping ASP largely consistent it's been broadly within the same line plus minus 10 percent the revenue growth over two years has been really amazing

adds.what: origin retail stores (per-store capex ~Rs 45-55 lakh; total ~Rs 3-3.3 cr incl. deposit and inventory), 29 operational, Jayanagar (Dec) and HSR Layout (early nex

growth.why: Management expects strong growth in Q3, Q4 and full year, backed by strong B2B order flow and US sell-through, ~USD 10-12 mn from newly onboarded accounts, and origin store expansion (29 stores, Jayanagar and HSR Layout planned), but no numeric full-year revenue guidance was given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose 176 bps YoY in Q2 to about 25% (Rs 736 mn on Rs 2,916.6 mn), and management said the new margin level is expected to sustain into Q3 under the hybrid casting model, excluding one-off regulatory refunds received in Q2.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Origin stores rose from 26 to 29 since the Q1 call, with Jayanagar (December) and HSR Layout (early next year) planned and expansion to pick up through end of Q4 FY27; B2B needs no significant capex, so the capacity signal is mainly retail stores.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects strong Q3, Q4 and full-year growth, with H1 revenue up 50% YoY, about USD 10-12 mn from newly onboarded accounts, and vendor consolidation by large US retailers driving share gains.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation was not disclosed, and B2B needs no significant capex, so a new capex announcement depends on the detailed FY28 origin store plan promised for the Q4 call; QIP is complete and funds are available.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management described Q3, Q4 and full-year outlook as strong, but gave no numeric full-year revenue or margin guidance to raise, and H1 revenue growth was 50%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Origin posted a Q2 loss of about Rs 3-3.5 crore, several new stores are still ramping, and the break-even of Rs 18-19 lakh monthly revenue is close to current levels, with the inventory build and currency exposure as watch items.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: New bracelet and necklace categories are being sampled, with entry into key US retailer accounts expected from Q4, plus CRM, website revamp and jewelry purchase plan being launched as origin sales enablers.

rows.label: International wholesale accounts (Middle East, Israel, Australia)
rows.why: About USD 10-12 mn of sales already from newly onboarded accounts, and the company is hiring new US sales agents to target 2-3 accounts.

rows.label: Origin store break-even and maturity
rows.why: Store-level break-even is about Rs 18-19 lakh monthly revenue, August was at break-even, and matured stores earn Rs 2-2.5 crore a year against a Rs 4-5 crore target, but Q2 origin loss was about Rs 3-3.5 crore.

rows.label: Interim dividend of Rs 2 per share
rows.why: Declared Rs 2 per share (100% of face value), totalling Rs 301.11 mn, with cash and investments of Rs 4,578.25 mn as of 30 Sep 2026.

tone.note: Management was confident on B2B growth, the Q3/Q4 outlook and margins, but cautious on origin ("a lot more to do") and evasive on order book and LGD certification; analysts pushed on the drivers of the sharp growth and the store economics.

quality.why: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 44% YoY to Rs 2,916.6 mn, driven by deeper share with existing US retailers as vendor consolidation shifts volume to Goldiam, plus new wholesale and international accounts (about USD 10-12 mn so far), with LGD pricing described as flat; the brief names no one-off gain, loss or weak base, and new-account contribution is described only as a kicker.
